method: Web research 2026-10-15 from search-engine summaries of the cited pages (pages not opened directly). Leave figures date from 2021-22 announcements.
overview: KPMG US is a Big Four firm. Its advisory business includes management consulting (strategy, operations, finance, people, customer) and deal advisory alongside risk and technology work; scans use KPMG's own US careers listing.

differentiators.text: KPMG built Lakehouse, a $450m learning and innovation campus in Lake Nona, Orlando (opened 2020), with in-person courses taught by partners and professionals each week.
differentiators.significance: Signals heavy investment in in-person training; how much new advisory hires use it was not confirmed.

early_career.text: Lakehouse was designed to deliver over a million hours of in-person professional development a year, mixing in-person and digital learning.
early_career.significance: Formal training capacity is large; new-hire curriculum details for advisory were not found.

employee_support.text: KPMG US announced 12 weeks' paid parental leave for all parents regardless of primary-caregiver status (up to 22 weeks combined with disability leave for birth parents) and up to three weeks of paid caregiver leave separate from PTO.
employee_support.significance: Caregiver leave for a family member's serious illness goes beyond standard benefits. Announced 2021-22; confirm current terms.

employee_support.text: Announced support includes up to $35,000 for fertility and $35,000 for adoption and surrogacy, 10 free counselling sessions a year and work/life coaching.

flexibility.text: KPMG introduced twice-yearly firm-wide breaks of at least nine consecutive days and a 'Flex with Purpose' hybrid approach.
flexibility.significance: Firm-wide breaks make it easier to actually disconnect. Hybrid alone is not evidence of flexibility.

unknowns: Whether the 2021-22 leave and break policies are unchanged in 2026.
Hours, travel and staffing model for NYC advisory associates.
